result: The authors obtained a cryo-EM map of CHIKV VLPs and reported resolutions of 4.6 Å (initial estimate) and 5.3 Å (verified resolution). The map was reconstructed from 36,236 particles and resolution was assessed using Fourier shell correlation criteria.
status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly questioned the resolution claim, stating 'The map resolution (4.6 Å) is likely to be an overestimate' and noting that 'At 4.6 Å, beta strands should be easily resolved throughout the map.' They requested additional validation procedures to reduce risk of over-fitting noise and anticipated 'the actual resolution will then turn out to be no better than 5 Å.' This indicates the reviewers accept the general quality but question the precise resolution value reported.

result: The authors fitted E1-E2 crystal structures into cryo-EM density and found that the four quasi-equivalent heterodimers within the VLP asymmetric unit are structurally more similar to each other than to the published crystal structure. The i3 trimers are more compact than q3 trimers, with differences in radius of gyration up to 5.8 Å and positional shifts of ~1.8 Å.
status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly praised this analysis as 'A technical highlight in this paper' and noted it 'led to the finding that the cryo-EM models of the relative positions of the domains of these proteins are consistent among the 4 quasi-equivalent heterodimers within the asymmetric unit of the icosaheral particle, but different from those of the crystal structures.' They affirmed that 'the molecular contacts between the subunits are more extensive in the cryo-EM structure than in the crystal structure' and drew a positive lesson about the merit of obtaining cryo-EM structures to reveal conformations 'free of potential crystallization artifacts.'

result: The CHK-152 antibody binds across domains B and A of E2, has the capacity to cross-link domain B with domain A, efficiently blocks viral fusion with host membranes, and likely neutralizes infection by stabilizing domain B and preventing exposure of the fusion loop on E1.
status_reasoning: Reviewers acknowledged the manuscript 'offers new insights at much higher resolution...into how the capsid interacts with neutralizing antibodies' and noted this is 'potentially of medical interest.' While they did not explicitly critique the CHK-152 mechanism claims, they accepted the overall antibody neutralization findings as part of the manuscript's contribution and did not raise concerns about these specific mechanistic interpretations.

result: The CHK-9, m10, and m242 antibodies bind near or at the receptor-attachment site on domain A of E2, with CHK-9 and m242 causing ~10 Å movement of domain B. These antibodies likely neutralize CHIKV infectivity by blocking the cellular binding site and limiting access to the cell surface receptor.
status_reasoning: Reviewers accepted the antibody-binding analysis as part of the manuscript's contribution to understanding 'how the capsid interacts with neutralizing antibodies,' which they noted is 'potentially of medical interest.' They did not raise specific concerns about the binding site mapping or proposed neutralization mechanisms for these antibodies, implicitly accepting these findings as part of the overall positive evaluation.

result: Four cryo-EM structures of CHIK VLPs complexed with Fab fragments (CHK-9, CHK-152, m242, m10) were determined to ~15 Å resolution, and crystal structures of CHK-9 and m242 Fab fragments were determined to 3.0 Å and 3.1 Å resolution, respectively. The E2 B domain showed different orientations in CHK-9 and m242 Fab-bound structures compared to non-complexed VLPs.
status_reasoning: Reviewers acknowledged the manuscript provides insights 'into how the capsid interacts with neutralizing antibodies' at lower resolution than the main VLP structure. They requested additional figures showing quality of fit but did not challenge the resolution estimates for the antibody complexes or the structural observations about domain B reorientation, indicating acceptance of these findings.

result: The CHIKV VLP structure shows a nucleocapsid core with 30 hexamers and 20 pentamers separated from E1-E2 ectodomains by a ~45 Å-wide lipid membrane with two leaflets separated by ~15 Å. The membrane is traversed by 240 pairs of α helices from E1 and E2. E3 glycoprotein was not observed, and E2 B-domain densities were weak.
status_reasoning: Reviewers did not raise concerns about these structural observations of the VLP architecture. They acknowledged the manuscript as 'a major advance' providing 'new insights at much higher resolution...into the virus capsid structure itself.' The request for figures showing quality of fit suggests they want to verify these details but does not indicate skepticism about the findings themselves.

result: A homology model of CHIKV NCP was generated based on SFV NCP crystal structure and fitted into the cryo-EM density. The NCP organization shows extensive contacts in hexameric capsomers around 2-fold axes with salt bridges between Lys178 and Glu240, but few contacts around 3-fold axes. The quasi-2- and 3-fold symmetry elements match almost perfectly between glycoprotein and NCP organization.
status_reasoning: Reviewers did not challenge the NCP modeling or the analysis of inter-molecular contacts. They acknowledged the manuscript provides new structural insights and their comment that 'The locations of individual subunits in an asymmetric unit have been shown in many previous studies' suggests they accept these findings but want more focused presentation on novel aspects rather than questioning the validity of the observations.

result: Comparison between VEEV and CHIK VLPs shows essentially the same overall radius, but positions and orientations of molecular protein components differ by up to 9.7 Å and 11.7°. The capsid proteins are more conserved in sequence but show the largest differences in position and orientation between the two viruses.
status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly requested that 'the authors should focus more on the structural differences between the two viruses' (referring to CHIKV and the previously published VEEV structure by Zhang et al., 2011). This indicates they accept the comparative analysis as valid and important, but want it emphasized more in the manuscript. They did not challenge the specific measurements or conclusions about structural differences.

result: The authors propose that blocking fusion requires binding only one E2 molecule per spike, while blocking receptor attachment requires blocking all three receptor-binding sites per spike, necessitating higher Fab concentrations for CHK-9, m10, and m242. The difference between MAb and Fab neutralization efficiency is attributed to bivalent attachment and cross-linking.
status_reasoning: Reviewers did not challenge these mechanistic interpretations about stoichiometric requirements for neutralization. They acknowledged the manuscript provides insights into 'how the capsid interacts with neutralizing antibodies' that are 'potentially of medical interest,' implicitly accepting the proposed mechanisms. The lack of specific critique of these logical inferences suggests reviewer acceptance.

result: The q3 spikes are translated ~1.8 Å away from the VLP center and may be poised to release E2 molecules for E1 fusogenic homotrimer formation. His170 does not interact closely with negatively charged residues for pH-sensing, while His256 contacts Glu166.
status_reasoning: Reviewers did not raise concerns about these structural observations or functional interpretations regarding spike differences and pH-sensing residues. These findings are part of the detailed structural analysis that reviewers acknowledged as providing 'new insights at much higher resolution' into the virus structure. The absence of critique suggests acceptance of these observations.

result: CHIK VLPs are structurally and immunologically indistinguishable from mature infectious virus, allowing structural studies to be performed without biosafety level 3 conditions.
status_reasoning: Reviewers did not question the use of VLPs as a model system or challenge the claim that VLPs are indistinguishable from infectious virus. They evaluated the manuscript based on the VLP structures without raising concerns about the validity of using VLPs as surrogates for infectious virus, implicitly accepting this experimental approach.
